returns.rationale: Klass getters return the address of a statically defined klass (transforms.c, keysdata.c, keysmngr.c, openssl/*.c); the generic getters forward to the loaded backend's static klass.
The process-wide klass registries filled by xmlSecInit and the registration functions; they live until xmlSecShutdown.
Lookups return a klass id stored in the list, i.e. a static klass.
The crypto function tables are static in the backend (openssl/crypto.c) and selected globally in dl.c; a loaded library's table lives until it is unloaded.
Process-wide settings owned by the library; the value stays valid until its setter replaces it.
String literals from static tables; xmlSecKeyDataGetIdentifier is deprecated and always returns NULL (keysdata.c).
Constructors and duplicators allocate an object the caller releases with the matching Destroy function, as their documentation states (keys.c, transforms.c, xmldsig.c, xmlenc.c, list.c, nodeset.c).

Each returns a newly created key: the lookups document that the caller destroys it (keysmngr.c), xmldsig.c destroys dsigCtx->signKey obtained from getKey, keyinfo.c destroys generated keys, and the loaders create the key they return.
Both create key data around an OpenSSL key (openssl/x509.c, openssl/evp.c).
GetChildren creates a set; Add and AddList link the new set into the ring of nset and return its head, which destroys the whole ring (nodeset.c).
Returns a newly created transform not yet added to a chain (transforms.c).
New libxml2 documents (parser.c, xmltree.c free them with xmlFreeDoc on their own error paths).
Documented as freed with xmlFree (base64.c, bn.c, xmltree.c); xmlSecGetNodeContentAndTrim returns the xmlNodeGetContent allocation.
The template root is created unlinked and the application is responsible for inserting it into a document (templates.c); until then it is freed with xmlFreeNode.
New libxml2 output buffers; xmlenc.c closes the one it creates with xmlOutputBufferClose.
A new libxml2 input buffer; parser.c frees it with xmlFreeParserInputBuffer.
New OpenSSL BIOs (openssl/crypto.c).
Returns a new reference to the OpenSSL key (openssl/evp.c).
The element leaves the list without being destroyed; the caller destroys it as the list's item klass would (list.c).
Template and tree helpers return a node linked into the tree of their first argument, or a string owned by that node; the document frees it.

Accessors return a member of their first argument: a context's result or chain element, a key's data, a buffer's bytes, a store's certificate (openssl/x509vfy.c returns the stack element without a reference).
Returns the first verified certificate from the certs stack it was given (openssl/x509vfy.c).

outputs.rationale: The klass writer allocates the buffer; keyinfo.c frees it with xmlFree.
The unlinked old node is handed to the caller instead of being freed (xmltree.c).
The former children are unlinked into a list handed to the caller instead of being freed (xmltree.c).
Hands out transform->outNodes, which the transform keeps (transforms.c).
An in/out cursor advanced to a following sibling in the same document.

adopts.rationale: Adopt functions take ownership of their last pointer argument on success (keys.c, keysmngr.c, transforms.c, openssl/evp.c, openssl/x509.c, openssl/x509vfy.c).
The key destroys its previous value and keeps the new one (keys.c).
The list destroys its items with its klass's destroyItem method (list.c).
The context destroys every transform of its chain (transforms.c).
The new set joins the ring destroyed with it (nodeset.c).
The child becomes part of the tree that frees it (xmltree.c).
The new node takes the old one's place in the tree that frees it (xmltree.c).
